title: Communication cost of the Newman protocol
statement:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be finite types, let $\Omega$ be a finite probability space, and let $p$ be a public-coin finite-message protocol over $\Omega$ with private inputs in $X$ and $Y$ and outputs in a type $\alpha$. Fix a target function $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$, real parameters $\varepsilon$ and $c$ with $c > 1$, and suppose that $p$ $\varepsilon$-computes $f$. Then the communication complexity of the associated Newman protocol equals
\[
  \left\lceil \log_2 t(X, Y, \varepsilon, c) \right\rceil + \mathrm{complexity}(p),
\]
where $t(X, Y, \varepsilon, c)$ is the derandomization sample count and $\mathrm{complexity}(p)$ is the communication complexity of $p$; that is, running the Newman protocol costs exactly the cost of $p$ together with the number of bits Alice needs to name one seed in the table of size $t(X, Y, \varepsilon, c)$.
hypotheses_covered: X and Y are finite types
Ω is a finite probability space
p is a public-coin finite-message protocol over Ω
f : X → Y → α is the target function
replaced:
If $p$ is a public-coin finite-message protocol that $\varepsilon$-computes $f$, and $c > 1$,
then the communication complexity of the Newman protocol equals
$\lceil \log_2(\mathtt{derandomizationSamples}\;X\;Y\;\varepsilon\;c) \rceil + p.\mathtt{complexity}$,
i.e.\ the original complexity plus the number of bits needed to index the seed table.
